title: Designing a Hybrid Neural System to Learn Real-world Crack Segmentation from Fractal-based Simulation (Cracktal / CAP-Net)
mechanism: Stochastic Koch-fractal crack simulator with exact labels. CAP-Net adds AdaIN style transfer and a pointwise-mutual-information branch with a consistency loss to bridge simulation and real data.
evidence: On SegCODEBRIM, a U-Net trained on 950 real multi-source images (F1 25.6%) did worse than a U-Net trained on simulation, which the authors attribute to inconsistent annotation styles across sources. CAP-Net adds +7% F1 over the simulation-trained U-Net. All images at 256 px.
adaptation: Our 5 sources with 5 label conventions are the same failure mode. Use fractal skeletons as a second generator alongside the dynamic-programming strands, and apply per-source intensity statistics (AdaIN-like) when rendering onto EL cells.
min_experiment: Add Cracktal skeletons as a second skeleton source in the procedural arm, 5 seeds. Metric: E1 relF1@2. Kill if not above the procedural arm alone.

alt_notes.adaptation: Second skeleton source in the procedural arm; per-source AdaIN-style intensity statistics when rendering.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Swap fractal skeletons into the procedural arm; kill if E1 relF1@2 not above DP skeletons.
